what: NDT-PACK (2026-10-17), measured and not kept: the pooled blocked GEMM's packed tiles reused between a thread's tasks, and the task orders that make reuse possible -- the blueprint's 'reuse panels where legal' (BCIR_Training_Architecture_Blueprint_2026-10-13, section 4, item 2). Every variant keeps the partition (the same tiles of C, each one task's, its K blocks in order), so every product is the same floats; only which tasks run together and what a thread keeps between them change. The reuse is legal by construction: one job's B is read-only for the job, and the cache's key is a per-job sequence number, never B's address, so a weight updated between steps is never served from an earlier pack.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207; AVX-512 with AVX512-BF16/FP16 and AMX; 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 a core, a 260 MB L3), the instance the container ran on after its 10:15 restart -- not ../update/'s 2.80 GHz one with 1 MB of L2 and 33 MB of L3; GCC 13.3, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); indicative wall times, no PMU

files.variants.py: the three arms as exact-match edits to a copy of runtime/c/bcir_tensor.c at d68e3d3 (python3 variants.py runtime/c OUT): colmajor (a job's task index walks one column block's row sets before the next; the kept order is row-major), cache (colmajor, and a thread keeps the AVX-512 kernel's packed tiles of one column block -- every K block, up to K = 1024 -- between the tasks of one job, keyed by a per-job sequence number, in a thread-local buffer: the measuring form of a caller-lent workspace), grp (tasks numbered in groups of the pool's thread count of column blocks, a group's row sets in turn, so the tasks that start together are distinct columns and a thread's next task is most often its last one's column)
